targets.review_note: Exploit integer axis-aligned geometry without rasterizing every cell. Sweep horizontal polygon edges: crossing an edge toggles the interior x-interval, represented by a clipped integer bitset. Only distinct edge heights change the row pattern. Count the 4-connected Euler characteristic from each adjacent-row transition: (one-black 2x2 corners minus three-black corners plus twice diagonal-two corners)/4. Repeated identical rows contribute zero, so large vertical gaps cost no work. The intersection has no holes: the complements of the simple polygon and the rectangle are both connected and meet outside a large enclosing box, hence their union (the intersection complement) is connected. Therefore the Euler characteristic equals the number of open black components. Use empty rows at the window bottom/top and exact clipped horizontal intervals; edge/point-only contacts do not create black area.
